review.verdict: The two intended vignettes have collapsed into one confusing center scene where the robot appears to receive the coins meant for the human painter, the "handprint" signature reads as an animal paw, and a clipped arm/box overlap plus a safe-area violation break the polish — this does not pass.
revisionNotes: Rebuild as the specified vertical-line diptych: left half shopper + framed painting, right half puzzler + robot, split by a thin line — currently all three figures are merged into one center scene with no divider.

The painting's signature renders as a pink claw/paw shape, not a human handprint — rebuild as five rounded finger ellipses over a palm so it doesn't read as an animal or robot mark under the 'NOT AI' tag.

The robot, not the shopper, is shown receiving the coins — move the coin prop so it changes hands between shopper and painting/seller only; the robot should instead be sliding the puzzle piece in beside the puzzler, as in the brief.
Fix the clipped/duplicated arm and the pink-striped box overlapping the puzzler's hand (looks like a gift, not a puzzle); separate the puzzle-piece prop from the limb so the shapes don't clip.
Pull 'puzzler' inward to about x 0.82 and drop scale toward 0.8 — lint flags it exiting the safe area at x 776–1067.
Drop the floating picture-frame/paw icon above the robot and keep only the counter-top painting from the brief; five main elements plus a disconnected icon is too crowded for one read.

review.verdict: Fails: the robot's arm crosses the center divider, the puzzle piece overlaps the robot's face, and the coins prop that carries the 'premium' idea is missing entirely — plus the split-diptych device repeats recent compositions too closely.
revisionNotes: Add back the coins prop at the shopper's hand (it's missing from the render) — without it the shopper is just pointing, and the whole 'pay a premium' idea has nothing to land on.
Shorten or redirect the robot's left arm; it currently crosses the center divider into the painting half, breaking the diptych split that defines the composition.
Move the puzzle component down and away from the robot's head — right now the pink piece overlaps the robot's face/smile, making that half read as clutter rather than 'robot slides piece in first'.
Nudge the shopper's pointing hand off the 'NOT AI' tag; the hand circle currently overlaps the start of the text.

Composition leans on the same thin-vertical-divider, blue/cream riso split used in several recent pieces — try a different divider device (counter edge, floor break, or offset panels) to differentiate it.

Consider a small low meter or dimmed color near the puzzler to visualize 'weakened ability to keep trying' from the phrase, since right now the second half only shows the robot winning, not the human's persistence draining.

review.verdict: The riso duotone rendering looks polished at a glance, but the two halves don't actually connect to their objects (painting floats apart from the shopper, robot arm overlaps the puzzler's body) and the meter is clipped at the edge, so the joke doesn't land in 3 seconds — this needs another pass before publishing.
revisionNotes: Left half reads as unrelated: the painting+NOT AI tag floats alone at the top while the shopper and coins sit far below on an empty platform. Pull the painting down to roughly x=0.28,y=0.55 and add a simple counter shape between shopper and frame so the coins visibly reach toward it.

Right half is muddled: the robot's raised arm and the puzzle piece overlap directly across the puzzler's torso/face, making it unclear who placed what. Scale the robot's arm/puzzle piece down and offset the puzzle board left of the puzzler so the piece slots into the board, not the person.

The thermometer meter is clipped at the right edge per the lint warning (x 1043…1074 outside safe area). Scale it down to ~0.3 and reposition inside the artboard, e.g. attach at x=0.78 instead of hugging the edge.

Brief calls for a riso diptych split by a thin vertical line; no divider is present, so the two scenes just float in a near-empty frame. Add the vertical rule and tighten the empty space in the upper-right quadrant.
The floating coin circles next to the shopper don't read as an offering gesture. Either attach them to an outstretched hand or move them onto the counter surface so the payment action is legible.

The split-screen human-vs-robot comparison is close to several recent sloppers' go-to layout; consider a more distinct staging (e.g. closer framing on the puzzle hand-off) so it doesn't blend into the pattern.
